text: The Iberian electricity market split on 2026-08-18 from 07:45Z to 15:15Z across 30 settlement intervals, with Portugal trading at a peak premium of 109.84 EUR/MWh above Spain (ENTSO-E A44 day-ahead). At the worst interval on 10:15Z, Portugal's price reached 110.73 EUR/MWh while Spain's fell to 0.89 EUR/MWh (ENTSO-E A44 day-ahead), imposing an extra import cost of 1,853,272.39 EUR on energy actually imported (A44 prices with A09 scheduled flows). The border operated at full capacity throughout the episode: at 10:15Z, the 3,330 MW net flow from Spain to Portugal matched the 3,330 MW available capacity exactly (ENTSO-E A09 scheduled exchanges and A61 day-ahead capacity). The Alcochete-Palmela transmission asset was unavailable at 2,800 MW due to planned maintenance, with 12 notices in force from publication on 2026-07-23 (ENTSO-E A78 transmission unavailability). The border being saturated is consistent with the price separation, though both follow from the same market coupling mechanism; A78 asset-level unavailability and A61 net border capacity are related but distinct quantities reflecting the operator's security assessment.

The Iberian electricity market split on 2026-08-19 from 07:30Z to 15:00Z, a 7.5-hour episode spanning 30 settlement intervals (ENTSO-E A44 day-ahead). Portugal faced a severe price premium of 108.16 EUR/MWh, reaching 110.16 EUR/MWh at the peak interval of 10:30Z, while Spain's price fell to 2 EUR/MWh at the same moment (ENTSO-E A44 day-ahead). The border between the two countries operated at full capacity throughout the episode: the Iberian interconnection was limited to 3,333 MW (ENTSO-E A61 day-ahead capacity), and scheduled flows from Spain to Portugal reached exactly 3,333 MW at peak (ENTSO-E A09 scheduled exchanges), with all 30 intervals showing saturation. The full border and the price separation are consistent with each other, both following from the market coupling mechanism, though this consistency does not establish causation. The Alcochete-Palmela transmission asset was unavailable due to planned maintenance at 2,800 MW capacity (ENTSO-E A78 transmission unavailability, notice published 2026-07-23), and 12 related notices were in force before the episode began; however, A78 asset-level data and A61 border-level capacity represent different quantities after the operator's security assessment, so the relationship between the maintenance and the 3,333 MW border limit cannot be directly equated. The price separation cost Portugal an estimated 1,473,528.35 EUR in extra import expenses (A44 prices with A09 scheduled flows).

The Iberian electricity market split on 2026-07-28 from 07:30Z to 14:15Z, a severe episode lasting 6.75 hours across 27 settlement intervals (ENTSO-E A44 day-ahead). Portugal traded at a peak premium of 77.8 EUR/MWh above Spain, reaching 80 EUR/MWh at 09:15Z while Spain fell to 2.2 EUR/MWh at the same interval (ENTSO-E A44 day-ahead). The border operated at full capacity throughout the episode: at the worst interval, the net flow from Spain to Portugal reached 4,275 MW, exactly matching the available border capacity (ENTSO-E A09 scheduled exchanges and A61 day-ahead capacity). The price separation imposed an extra import cost of 356,136.98 EUR on energy actually imported into Portugal (A44 prices with A09 scheduled flows). An unplanned outage of the Pereiros-Rio Maior 1 transmission asset, with 3,600 MW normally available, was among five notices in force during the episode, published from 2026-06-25 (ENTSO-E A78 transmission unavailability). The border being saturated is consistent with the price separation, though both follow from market coupling mechanics rather than one causing the other; additionally, the A78 asset-level constraint and the A61 net border capacity are related but distinct quantities reflecting the operator's security assessment.
